title: Water and wastewater rates approved; transit study advances
subtitle: Also: community engagement strategy, 2026 debt plan, Elora paid parking launch, heritage designations and Elora BIA appointments.
overview: Council approved the 2025 Water and Wastewater Rate Study and the related financial plans {{vote:m3}}. The study recommends annual volume rate increases of 3.0% for water and 2.0% for wastewater, and removing connection charges from 2026. The proposed rates will return in future draft budgets, so residents will see final figures during budget deliberations. The financial plans go to the provincial environment ministry as a licence requirement.

Council also received a progress report on the Transit Feasibility Study {{vote:m2}}, with a second round of public engagement planned for winter 2026. It endorsed including debt requirements and capacity in the 2026 staff draft budget {{vote:m5}} and received an update on paid parking in downtown Elora {{vote:m6}}. Staff are targeting an early January 2026 launch, with free resident parking through a registration portal.

Council directed staff to gather feedback on the draft Community Engagement Charter and Strategy through Connect CW and bring a final report on December 15, 2025 {{vote:m4}}. Consent items approved included heritage designations for three Fergus properties, a demolition request for a listed Salem property, and a part lot control exemption {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2025 rate study and financial plans, directed the proposed rates into future draft budgets, and sent the financial plans to the provincial environment ministry.
Council received a progress report on the study, which is weighing three service concepts before a second round of public engagement.
Council received the draft report and directed staff to collect feedback through Connect CW and return with a final report on December 15, 2025.
Council approved including the debt requirements and capacity outlined in report COR2025-67 in the 2026 staff draft budget.
Council received the report on the phase one paid parking program for downtown Elora, targeted to go live in early January 2026.
Council approved consent items, including designation of 219 Farley Road, 298 Union Street East and 300 St. Andrew Street West in Fergus, and demolition of a listed Salem dwelling.

decisions.item: Elora BIA board and related by-laws
decisions.detail: Council passed by-laws appointing the Elora BIA board and designating the three Fergus heritage properties, plus a part lot control exemption.

debate: On the rate study, one councillor asked to present the wastewater increase as 1% instead of 2% and raised the increase for Bridge Street properties. The mayor and staff said alternate rates could be considered in budget deliberations, and the mover accepted that.

Councillors asked why properties must connect to both water and wastewater. Staff said wastewater billing relies on water meter data and that connecting to both is the preference in the by-law, with exceptions.

On the 219 Farley Road designation, a councillor questioned the building's future use. Staff said the zoning was set up to allow varied uses and the subdivision was designed around the house. Designation also opens heritage grants and strengthens property standards powers.

On transit, councillors asked about linking on-demand rural service to GO connections, involving the County's Ride Well service, and funding sources such as the Ontario Transit Investment Fund, gas tax and development charges. Staff confirmed no transit costs are in the debt forecast.

On paid parking, councillors worried about resident confusion over the three-hour limit, staff capacity, signage and a grace period. Staff said a licensing coordinator is being hired and signage is adequate, and no grace period has been planned. Communications staff will hold in-person help sessions, including at the seniors centre.
